caption:
Every Custom HTML tag in your GTM container can read your forms, cookies and checkout.
Most businesses don’t know what half of theirs actually do.

Why it’s a risk
→ It runs any JavaScript, with no permission review
→ One bad vendor snippet can leak customer data or break checkout
→ It’s the hardest kind of tag to debug when tracking fails

What we do instead
1. Replace Custom HTML with Community Template Gallery templates
2. Turn your own code into custom templates — sandboxed, with declared permissions
3. Block risky tag types with gtm.blocklist
4. Every Custom HTML tag that stays needs an owner and a reason

caption:
Is your website built with React, Vue or Next.js?
GA4 might be counting every page view twice.

Why it happens
→ The URL changes without a real page load
→ GA4 enhanced measurement sends a page_view on the history change
→ A manual virtual page view in GTM sends another one

The fix: one source of truth
1. Choose who sends page_view — GA4 history tracking OR your data layer, never both
2. Push a virtual_page_view event after each route change
3. Turn off “Page changes based on browser history events” in GA4
4. Test in Preview: 3 routes = exactly 3 page_view events

Running an SPA and not sure your numbers are right?
Comment "SPA" and we'll check your single-page app for double page views. Prefer private? Send us a message.

caption:
12 GA4 tags in your container?
You probably need one.

The problem
A separate tag for add_to_cart, begin_checkout and purchase — then copies for staging and a second property. Every change has to be made in a dozen places, and one always gets missed.

The fix: build once, make it dynamic
1. One GA4 Event tag with Event Name = {{Event}}
2. One Custom Event trigger with RegEx: ^(view_item|add_to_cart|begin_checkout|purchase)$
3. “Send Ecommerce data” switched on
4. A RegEx Table on {{Page Hostname}} picks the right Measurement ID for live and staging

Fewer tags. Fewer mistakes. Every change in one place.

caption:
Google Ads shows fewer sales than your store?
Enhanced Conversions can close part of that gap.

Why sales go missing
→ Cookies get blocked or expire
→ Customers switch devices before they buy
→ Google can’t connect the ad click to the sale — so Smart Bidding under-values your best campaigns

How we set it up in GTM
1. Turn on Enhanced Conversions in Google Ads and accept the customer data terms
2. Create a User-Provided Data variable from the data layer — not from the page
3. Clean the data first: trim spaces, lowercase emails, phone numbers in +880 format
4. The Google tag hashes everything with SHA-256 — no raw email leaves the browser
5. Check the Diagnostics tab after a few days

caption:
Server-side GTM isn’t only for sending more data.
It’s the best tool for sending less.

The problem
Forms and checkouts push email, phone and names into the data layer. Browser pixels forward whatever they get — sometimes personal data into GA4 (not allowed), or full IP addresses to vendors that don’t need them.

The fix: Transformations in server-side GTM
1. Route vendors through your server container
2. Exclude email, phone and name before the GA4 tag
3. Allow only a short list of fields for each vendor
4. Send hashed data only where it’s needed — like Meta CAPI matching
5. Keep a simple data map: which platform gets which field

You control the data. Not the vendor’s script.

caption:
GTM isn’t slowing your website down.
The tags you fire on “All Pages” are.

The problem
Every browser pixel loads its own JavaScript. Many fire on every page even when they’re only needed at checkout — plus old heatmaps, ended tests and agency leftovers. Core Web Vitals drop, and your ads and SEO pay for it.

The fix: a lean container
1. List every tag on All Pages and ask: does it need every page?
2. Narrow triggers — checkout pixels only on checkout
3. Delete dead tags and unused vendors
4. Move pixels to server-side GTM: one request from the browser, many platforms from the server
5. Measure before and after with PageSpeed Insights

Site speed is a tracking problem too.

caption:
Most people open GTM Preview mode just to see if a tag fired.
Here are 7 things it can do that save hours of debugging.

1. Click the event, not Summary — see variable values at that exact moment
2. Data Layer tab — the merged state after every push
3. Click a fired tag — the exact values it sent
4. Consent tab — consent state on every event
5. Errors tab — tag errors you’ll never see on the page
6. Share — send a preview link to your developer or client
7. Server preview side by side — follow one hit from browser to every platform

This week: custom templates, SPA page views, dynamic tags, Enhanced Conversions, server-side transformations and site speed.

caption:
Your ecommerce data can be right on one page and wrong on the next.
The reason is often one missing line.

Why it happens
→ dataLayer.push() adds data, it doesn't replace it
→ Old items from the last event stay in the object
→ Reports then show the wrong products or values

The fix
1. Push { ecommerce: null } before every ecommerce event
2. Then push the new event with its own items
3. Check each event in GTM Preview, not just the first one

caption:
Your tags can fire before the visitor has chosen anything.
Consent Mode v2 sets the rules before the first tag loads.

Four signals to set
→ ad_storage: ad cookies
→ ad_user_data: user data sent to Google for ads
→ ad_personalization: personalized ads
→ analytics_storage: GA4 cookies

Set them to "denied" by default.
Change to "granted" only after the visitor's choice.

caption:
A price of "BDT 1,200.00" is text, not a number.
GA4 and ad platforms can't sum text correctly.

A simple Custom JavaScript variable fixes it
→ Remove symbols, commas and letters
→ Turn the rest into a number
→ Return 0 if the value is missing

Examples
"BDT 1,200.00" → 1200
"$49.90" → 49.9

Test this on one purchase in Preview before you roll it out.

caption:
setTimeout(…, 2000) is a guess.
It's slow on some devices and breaks on slow networks.

Use tag sequencing instead
1. Setup tag: loads your config first
2. Event tags: wait until setup is finished
3. Cleanup tag: runs last and clears temporary values

It's set in the tag's Advanced settings.
No timers, no guessing.

caption:
Testing changes on your live website?
Your customers see every mistake you make.

GTM Environments fix this
→ Live: your real website
→ Staging: QA and client review
→ Development: your own test sandbox

The workflow
1. Build the change in the Staging environment
2. Test the full path on a staging site
3. Publish to Live only when it passes

6. Version named, with a clear note
7. Full path checked in Preview: form, cart, purchase

caption:
Your tag fired, but at the wrong moment?
Timing is often the reason.

The three built-in moments
→ gtm.js: the GTM script has loaded
→ gtm.dom: the HTML is parsed and ready
→ gtm.load: the page is fully loaded, images included

Pick the earliest moment your tag really needs.
Too late means lost data. Too early means missing elements.

Your lead numbers look better than your real leads.

→ Wait for Tags: holds the page until the tag has sent

Scroll Depth shows you how far they got.

→ 50%: reached the middle
→ 75%: reading the offer
→ 90%: near the end

Use it on long pages where scrolling matters.

GTM user roles

→ Edit: change tags, but cannot publish
→ Approve: review changes before they go live
→ Publish: push changes to Live

Keep Publish access with one or two trusted people.
